I'm rarely late.

original: 目覚ましかけ忘れてて、仕事に遅刻しちゃった。

en.text: I was late for work because I forgot to set my alarm.
I forgot to set my alarm and was late for work.

original: 遅刻の常習犯だよね？

en.text: She's always late, isn't she?
He's always late, isn't he?

original: 週に3回遅刻とか、あり得ないですよね？

en.text: Being late three times in one week — isn't that unbelievable?

original: 遅刻するのやめてもらえます？

en.text: Can you please stop being late all the time?

original: 日本人は遅刻にシビアだ。

en.text: Japanese people do not take kindly to being late.
Japanese people are strict about coming on time.

original: 遅刻しちゃうかと思った。

en.text: I thought that I was going to be late.

original: 遅刻しようものなら、上司にクビ切られるのは確実だな。

en.text: The boss will surely fire you if you're late.

original: 彼女は学校に遅刻しそうになった。

en.text: She was almost late for school.

original: 毎日毎日遅刻しやがって。たまには俺より早く来たらどうだ。

en.text: You're always late. Why don't you come in before me every once in a while?
You are late every single day. Why don't you come in earlier than me sometime?

original: 遅刻だ。メアリーに殺されちゃう。

en.text: I'm late. Mary is going to kill me.

original: 初日から、遅刻なんてヤダぁ。

en.text: I don't want to be late for class on the first day.

original: 寝坊して遅刻しそうになった。

en.text: They slept in and it looks like they might be late.
I overslept and I was almost going to be late.

original: 日本人は遅刻にうるさい。

en.text: Japanese people are annoyed by tardiness.

original: いつも遅刻しちゃうのよ。

en.text: Unfortunately, I'm always late.
